events.speaker: SOL — flat
events.text: You walked in through the west gate. Nobody walks in through the west gate.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: So either you don't know this place, or you know it well enough not to care. Which?

choices.text: I know it. I used to survey it.
I know the air. That's all I need to know.
I'm passing through.

events.text: I know it. I used to survey it.

events.speaker: SOL — hard
events.text: Surveyed it. For them.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: Then you know exactly how much good a survey does. I've got a hundred and six people in these three blocks and not one of them has ever been helped by a line on a map.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: What do you want?

choices.text: Teodor Marsh. He sent for me.
A place to stand for a night. I'll work for it.
I'm looking into what happened at Cellar Row.

events.text: I'm looking into what happened at Cellar Row.

events.speaker: SOL — quiet
events.text: Cellar Row.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: Nine people. I was on the third floor of Pell when it went. We heard nothing. That's the thing nobody understands about the black — there's nothing to hear.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: If you're here to write a report about it eighteen months late, you can turn round.

choices.text: I'm here to publish what was in the data.
I'm here because I should have said something at the time.

events.text: I'm here because I should have said something at the time.

events.speaker: SOL — quiet
events.text: ...Say that again.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text:
No. Don't. I heard you.
 Here's what I'll do with that: nothing. Not today. Today you're a pair of hands and I am short of hands. We'll have the other conversation when there's time, and there is never time.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: Right. You want to stand in my courtyard, you're on the rota. Nobody sleeps below the second floor. Nobody goes into the yard after dark without a light. And if the meter goes over eight hundred you go up, you don't go home.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: Marsh is at the Arcade, down Marrow. Mind the Slip.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: That's the third time this month. They're not after the food.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text:
And that was your shift, by the way. I put you on the rota an hour ago and you did a barrel watch with a prybar, which is not what the rota says, and I have marked it down as done.
 Nobody gets to stand in this yard and not be on it. Not even you.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: They're after cartridges. Which tells you what's happening out there better than any survey.

choices.text: Where are they coming from?
How many filters do you have left?

events.text: Where are they coming from?

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: Ash crews. They strip the empty blocks — copper, cable, anything. When the buildings run out they come for people. There's no mystery in it. Hungry is hungry.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: Go and see him. And Vasko —

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: Yes, I know your name. Everybody in this yard knows your name. Some of them are being polite about it.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text:
Take this. Thirty metres of line and a descender. It was in the ambulance and the ambulance is not coming back.
 If you go up — and you will go up, everyone does eventually — you want a way down that is not falling.

events.speaker: TEO — dry
events.text: Vasko.

events.speaker: TEO
events.text: You took your time. I posted that in March.

choices.text: It went to an address I hadn't lived at for a year.
I read it in March. It took me until now to get on a train.
You could have written your name on it.

events.text: I read it in March. It took me until now to get on a train.

events.speaker: TEO
events.text: That's about right. That's about what I'd have done.

events.speaker: TEO
events.text: You'll want to know why I sent it.

events.speaker: TEO
events.text:
Bek gave that letter to me to post. Eleven days before. I put it in my coat and I forgot it, because I was sixty-one years old and I was tired and it was a Thursday.
 I found it again in a coat I hadn't worn since the funeral.

choices.text: What was he like?
You could have burned it.
[Say nothing]

events.text: What was he like?

events.speaker: TEO — quiet
events.text:
Ilya? Careful. Kept a rain gauge on his own roof for sixteen years because he did not think the published one was sited properly.
 He was right about that too. It changed nothing. He knew it would change nothing and he kept the gauge.

events.speaker: TEO — quiet
events.text: So. Now there are two of us who didn't do the small thing at the time.

choices.text: That's not the same.
No. There are two of us.
What do you want me to do about it?

events.text: No. There are two of us.

events.speaker: TEO — quiet
events.text: ...Aye.

events.speaker: TEO
events.text: A letter proves a man was worried.

events.speaker: TEO
events.text:
You need the raw log. Not the published line — the numbers the line was drawn against.
 Nine heads. Weekly. Three years. In their own hand.

events.speaker: TEO
events.text: It's in the instrument hut at Vent Field 9. Past the Cut. Past a lot of things.

choices.text: Why haven't you got it yourself?
I know the field. I calibrated half those heads.
What's it worth to you?

events.text: I know the field. I calibrated half those heads.

events.speaker: TEO
events.text: I know you did. That's rather the point of you.

events.speaker: TEO
events.text: Take this. It's the field manual — yours, actually, you left it in the hut. There's an annexe in the back on reading a draw off a single head. You wrote it. You'd forgotten you wrote it.

events.speaker: TEO
events.text: Mind the Slip. And Vasko — go over it, not round it. Round it takes you through the low ground on Kell and Kell will have you.

events.speaker: OSTROWSKI
events.text: Don't come closer. I've got a bar and I will use it badly.

events.speaker: OSTROWSKI
events.text:
...You're not a crew. Crews don't knock.
 There's four of us. My wife's on the first floor, she doesn't come down any more. The two kids sleep up there too.

choices.text: Your air down here is at eleven hundred. Why are you still on the ground floor?
Do you know why it's got worse?
[Give a filter]

events.text: Your air down here is at eleven hundred. Why are you still on the ground floor?

events.speaker: OSTROWSKI
events.text: Because the workshop's down here and the workshop is how we eat. I do two hours and I go up. I know what I'm doing. I've lived on this street forty years.

events.speaker: OSTROWSKI
events.text: If you're going west, tell whoever's up there that there's four of us. That's all. Just the number.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: Still here.

events.speaker: SOL — flat
events.text: You've been west.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: Say it, then. You've been holding it in your mouth since you came through the gate.

choices.text: You cracked three borehole heads. You're pulling the field through Fenn Street.
There are still people living down there. I met them.
I'm not here to judge it. I want to understand it.

events.text: You cracked three borehole heads. You're pulling the field through Fenn Street.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text:
Yes. I cracked them. I wedged them open with a bar and a rag and I did it myself so that if it ever comes back on anyone it comes back on me.
 Do you want the arithmetic or do you want to be angry first? I can wait.

choices.text: Give me the arithmetic.
You're doing exactly what Krajcik does. Just smaller.
Nothing. I just needed to hear you say it.

events.text: Give me the arithmetic.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text:
A hundred and six here. Eleven there. The heads pull about nine hundred parts off my courtyard overnight and put about eleven hundred onto Fenn Street. Fenn Street is upstairs-capable; every building down there has a first floor and every one of those eleven people knows to use it. My courtyard is where the water is, the generator is, and the only clear ground for two blocks.
 If I shut the heads, I lose the yard. If I lose the yard I lose the block inside a fortnight.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text:
You'll do what you'll do. You've got a bar and you know which way the wedges came out. I'm not going to stand in front of them.
 Just don't tell me it was easy afterwards.

events.speaker: REN
events.text:
Three heads, cracked and wedged. Two turns each with the bar and the draw reverses.
 Fenn Street comes down to about three hundred. The Stacks courtyard goes up to about nine.

choices.text: [Shut the vents] Fenn Street can't go upstairs forever.
[Leave them] A hundred and six against eleven.
[Half-measure] Shut one. Split the difference.

events.text: [Shut the vents] Fenn Street can't go upstairs forever.

events.speaker: REN
events.text: Done. Two turns each.

events.speaker: TEO
events.text: Let me see it.

events.speaker: TEO
events.text:
...Four hundred and six degrees at 9-3, week of the eleventh of July. And the line they printed that quarter has Cellar Row two hundred metres clear.
 They didn't get it wrong. You can't get four hundred degrees wrong.

events.speaker: TEO — quiet
events.text: Now. What's it for?

choices.text: Publish it. All of it, with names.
Use it. Make them cut the trench in the right place.
I don't know yet.

events.text: Publish it. All of it, with names.

events.speaker: TEO
events.text: Then be certain. Publishing voids the contract. Voiding the contract stops the money. Stopping the money stops whatever it is Krajcik is actually doing with it, and I have never been able to work out what that is, only that four hundred households have quietly stopped being here.

events.speaker: TEO
events.text: Go east. Field Office Two. And Vasko — whatever you decide, decide it before you're standing in front of him. He is very good at being reasonable at people.

events.speaker: IRIS
events.text: You can't be — you're not supposed to be past the barrier, this is a restricted —

events.speaker: IRIS — shaken
events.text: ...Ren.

events.speaker: IRIS
events.text:
Sorry. Sorry, that was — hello. Hello.
 You look well. That's a stupid thing to say. Nobody looks well here, the particulate does something to everyone's skin.

choices.text: Hello, Iris.
You're signing the lines now.
I need to get into the office.

events.text: Hello, Iris.

events.speaker: IRIS
events.text: You're the first person to say my name in eleven weeks who wasn't reading it off a form.

events.speaker: IRIS
events.text: Yes. Survey Engineer Two. I got your job, technically. Nobody says that but it's technically true.

events.speaker: IRIS
events.text:
I do the field work and the reduction and I put the line where the reduction puts it, and then the reduction goes upstairs and the line that comes back down is not always the line I sent up.
 I have a folder. Of the differences. I don't know why I keep it. It isn't evidence of anything except that I noticed.

choices.text: How long?
Then say something.
I kept one too. For eleven months.

events.text: How long?

events.speaker: IRIS
events.text: Two years and ten months. Since before you were hired.

events.speaker: IRIS
events.text: Why are you here? Actually here.

choices.text: I have the raw borehole log.
There's an order for a full trench cut. Signed and never issued. I want it.
To finish what I should have done.

events.text: I have the raw borehole log.

events.speaker: IRIS
events.text: You went into Field 9. On foot. With a cartridge.

events.speaker: IRIS
events.text: God, that's the most Ren thing I've ever heard.

events.speaker: IRIS — quiet
events.text: I could give you my pass.

events.speaker: IRIS
events.text:
...I could. I'm not going to.
 I have eleven months on this contract and a mother in a place that costs four hundred a month and I am not — I can't be the one who —
 There's a service door on the north elevation. The hasp is rusted through. I'm not telling you that. I'm saying it out loud in a yard.

events.speaker: IRIS
events.text:
He'll be in there. He's always in there. He'll be very nice to you.
 ...One more thing. The ash crews out at the field — the big ones with the hammers. They plant the back foot before they swing. Every time, about half a second early. I have watched them from that window for two years and I have never seen one not do it.

events.speaker: KRAJCIK
events.text: Miss Vasko. Sit down if you like. There's a chair, it's the only one, it's not comfortable.

events.speaker: KRAJCIK
events.text: You have the July log. You have the cut order. I'd rather we skipped the part where I pretend otherwise, because it's undignified and we're both tired.

choices.text: You knew Cellar Row was inside the burn.
You signed a trench order and buried it.
I'm not here to arrest you. I want to understand it.

events.text: You knew Cellar Row was inside the burn.

events.speaker: KRAJCIK
events.text:
Yes.
 Would you like me to say it more slowly? Yes. Cellar Row was inside the burn. The published line was wrong. Nine people died because of a document I am responsible for.

events.speaker: KRAJCIK
events.text: Second drawer. It is not locked. It has never needed to be.

events.speaker: REN
events.text:
A removals ledger. Handwritten, one line per household, ruled by somebody who rules lines for a living.
 Three hundred and forty entries. Deposit, removal, twelve months' rent, and a column headed SCHEME that is empty the whole way down.

choices.text: There's no scheme.
Where does the money come from?

events.text: There's no scheme.

events.speaker: KRAJCIK
events.text:
No. There is a Directorate paper from four years ago that recommends one, and a line in the estimates where it would go, and nothing in the line.
 I write to them every April. I have the replies. They are extremely courteous.

events.speaker: KRAJCIK
events.text:
The margin. On a contract to manage a fire that cannot be managed.
 That is the whole trick and you have just found it in about nine seconds.

events.speaker: KRAJCIK
events.text:
I am not asking you to think I am a good man. I'm asking you to do the determination I am required to make every quarter and make every morning anyway.
 If you publish, the contract voids inside a fortnight. The Authority withdraws. The relocation stops. Four hundred and six people are still in Hollis and there is no longer anybody in the world whose job it is to move them.

choices.text: Then issue the cut order and take the consequences.
You don't get to make that choice for them.
What do you want from me?
How many did you move after you knew?

events.text: Then issue the cut order and take the consequences.

events.speaker: KRAJCIK
events.text:
And on the day the excavator breaks ground on a line that is not the published line, every solicitor within two hundred miles will ask why.
 I have thought about it every day for fourteen months. I have not found the version where it works.

events.speaker: KRAJCIK
events.text: Here is what I can offer you, and I want you to notice that it is not a bribe.

events.speaker: KRAJCIK
events.text:
Come back. Survey Engineer One, my authority, your line. You redraw the boundary honestly, quarter by quarter, and I move the households on the inside of it first. Nobody is told. The contract survives. The money keeps moving.
 You would be lying, continuously, for years, and you would be saving roughly thirty households a quarter while you did it.

choices.text: No. It goes on the record.
I'll take it.
I'll take it. [Lie]
Issue the cut order and I'll put it on the right line for you.

events.text: No. It goes on the record.

events.speaker: KRAJCIK
events.text:
I thought so. I would have been disappointed if you hadn't, which is an absurd thing for me to feel and I feel it anyway.
 The trench crews start on the published line at first light. I can't stop that now; it's three contracts deep. I'd stay out of the Cut.

events.speaker: KRAJCIK
events.text:
One more thing, and then I'll let you go.
 The nine at Cellar Row. I have their names on a card in my wallet. I don't show people; it's not for that. I just wanted you to know it's there, because I think you're about to decide that I don't carry it.
 I carry it. I simply carry it and keep working. So do you.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: Still here.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: Sit down. You're grey.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text:
You got some of them. That's the job. The job is not everybody, it has never been everybody, and anyone who tells you it is has not done it.
 You'll want to give me the names of the ones you didn't. Don't. I already have them. I write them down before I need to.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: Now. The Authority has plant on the road at Kell. That is tomorrow's problem and it is coming tonight.

events.speaker: SOL — flat
events.text:
It was my yard, Vasko. My yard, at four in the morning, because of three borehole heads that a month ago were doing their job.
 I am telling you that as a fact, not as a knife. I have to be able to say the true shape of a thing out loud or I stop being able to do this.

events.speaker: SOL
events.text: Get some water in you.

events.speaker: NESSA
events.text: Sol says you've got the borehole log.

events.speaker: NESSA
events.text:
She says it proves they knew. Which — good. Fine. That's what everyone's always said and now there's paper.
 I want to read it.

choices.text: [Give her the log]
Before you do — the July sheet has my initials on it.
It's not ready. Not yet.

events.text: Before you do — the July sheet has my initials on it.

events.speaker: NESSA
events.text: What?

events.speaker: REN
events.text:
I checked the July sheet. I saw four hundred and six degrees at 9-3 and I saw the line they were about to print, and I knew those two things could not both be true.
 I raised it with nobody. I had eleven months left on a contract and I told myself somebody senior would catch it.
 Four months later your father died in his kitchen.

events.speaker: NESSA
events.text:
Why are you telling me?
 No — genuinely. Why now. Is it so I say something that makes it easier? Because I'm not going to. I don't have that.

choices.text: I'm not telling you so you'll say anything. I'm telling you because it's yours.
Because you'd have found it in the log tonight, and I wanted you to hear it from me.
I don't know. Maybe so I'd stop carrying it.

events.text: I'm not telling you so you'll say anything. I'm telling you because it's yours.

events.speaker: NESSA
events.text:
...Yeah.
 Yeah, all right.
 Go and do something with it. That's the only thing that's any use to me now. Don't stand there.

events.speaker: NESSA
events.text: They're cutting the trench tomorrow. Did you know that? Everyone's talking about it like it's weather.

events.speaker: REN
events.text:
The excavators are idling on the published line. Krajcik is standing on the spoil heap with a clipboard he is not reading. Forty people are watching from the far side, because it is the largest thing that has happened in Hollis in a year.
 I am carrying the log, the order, and the July sheet with my initials in the check box.

events.speaker: KRAJCIK
events.text: Miss Vasko. You are standing where the spoil goes.

events.speaker: KRAJCIK — quiet
events.text:
There is no entry against your name for the fourteenth. I looked, because I am the sort of man who looks.
 You came in off the north elevation, which means somebody told you the hasp was gone, which means somebody in my office decided you should be in it. I have not asked who and I am not going to.

events.speaker: REN
events.text: Forty people. A man on a heap of spoil. Every true sentence I have and about nine seconds to pick one.

choices.text: Put it on the record. All of it, including me.
Make him cut it on the true line, openly.
choices.why: He told you to ask him in front of them. You never asked.

choices.text: Take the desk. Draw the line honestly and tell nobody.
Burn it. Use their own lorries and empty Hollis.
choices.why: Sol would have to run it with you, and you have not stood in front of her since the water came up.

choices.text: Walk away. Take it with me.

events.text: Put it on the record. All of it, including me.

events.speaker: REN
events.text: I walk to the far side, where the forty people are, and I start with my own name.

events.title: ON THE RECORD
paragraphs: You put it on the record. All of it — the log, the order, the July sheet with your own initials in the check box.

The contract voided in eleven days. The Authority withdrew its plant on a Tuesday, and the trench, which was never going to work where they were cutting it, stopped at a hundred and forty metres and is still there.
Hollis burned faster after that. Everybody knew why. It turns out that matters more than people say it does, and less than you hoped.
You were charged as a party to it. Nine counts. The hearing took four days and your evidence took two of them, and at no point in it did you say that you had been young, or tired, or under contract.
1 of the names you read out were people you had carried as far as a stairwell in a filling street four days earlier, and not far enough.

The Stacks courtyard is in the record too. You put it there yourself: the date, the three heads, the bar, the wedge, and the name of the person who turned them. Sol did not attend. She sent a note through Marsh that said only *right*, and it is the shortest and least kind letter anyone has ever sent you.

You put two Authority men and a scavenger on the ground getting in. That was in the record too. Your counsel wanted it framed as necessity and you would not let her, because it was not necessity, it was nine minutes and a temper.
You had already said it out loud, by then, to nearly everyone it belonged to. The hearing was not the hard part. The hearing was the last part.
Nessa came. She sat at the back with her arms folded and she did not look at you and she came every single day.
She wrote to you afterwards. One line: *You didn't make me find out on my own. That's the whole letter.*
The Ostrowskis got out. All four. He wrote down your name on the back of a docket at the relocation office and spelled it wrong and would not be corrected.

The Stacks lost the courtyard in a fortnight, exactly as Sol said they would. They moved the generator to the second floor of Pell and the rota got harder and they did not lose anybody, which Sol has never once called luck.
Teodor Marsh closed the exchange and went to his sister's. He posted you one letter, on time, and it said only: *That was the small thing. Done now.*
3 minutes in Hollis. You lifted the meter 2 times. 3 people up a stairwell.
